audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Rumble six of seven stages, but the whys underneath it say the opposite: whys[3] 'the edge evens out', whys[4] 'neither side dominates clean', whys[5] 'it stays Skill', whys[6] 'two tank items and Permafrost CC uptime outlast everything Rumble can output'. The already-audited mirror (audits/top/rumble__sejuani.json) states Rumble takes levels 2-3, it evens 4-5, and Sejuani owns two items.
audit.why: The chart contradicts both its own explanations and the opposing page.
audit.corrected: Levels 1, 4-5 and first item should read Skill and two items should read Sejuani. I did not write these as edits — a side value cannot change without breaking the +/-10% length band ('Rumble' to 'Sejuani' is +16.7%), so this needs the applier or mirror-fix to set it. Raised in questionsForUser.

audit.why: Spikes at Rumble 2-3, Sejuani 6, Sunfire and late match the mirror's staging. The 2-3 spike now names Electro Harpoon's magic-resist shred, which is what actually makes his early poke hurt.

audit.whatIsWrong: 1) Ability slots are wrong in two places: wants.you[0] calls Flamespitter '(W)' and wants.you[1] calls Scrap Shield '(E)'. Flamespitter is Q, Scrap Shield is W, Electro Harpoon is E. 2) Electro Harpoon does not appear anywhere on the page, despite being his only ranged tool, carrying two charges, slowing, and reducing magic resist. 3) Junkyard Titan's Overheat is never mentioned: at 100% heat he gains attack speed but cannot cast spells at all — the cleanest engage window in the matchup. 4) Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants immunity to slows, so Electro Harpoon's slow does nothing until a hit has broken the armour. The mirror already establishes this from the Rumble side.
audit.why: Two mislabelled slots, his main poke absent, and the two windows that decide when you may press Arctic Assault (Overheat, and Frost Armor holding) both missing.
audit.corrected: Slots fixed, Electro Harpoon named with its shred and slow, Overheat named as the cast-lockout window, and Frost Armor's slow immunity stated in the same terms the mirror uses.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names only Scrap Shield and gives no seconds.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is 6s flat — short enough that waiting it out is not a plan by itself; Overheat and Equalizer's 130s are the windows worth naming.

audit.whatIsWrong: Overheat's cast lockout and Frost Armor's slow immunity were both absent.
audit.why: They are the two facts that turn this from a poke lane you endure into a lane with scheduled windows.
audit.corrected: Added to mid, early and spikes[0].

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin flip of who steps up first — take W, last-hit, and give him nothing; his Flamespitter at level 1 is short range but punishing if you stand in it. At level 2 he spikes harder than you: Flamespitter into overheat autos beats your raw auto pattern with no Frost stacks, so use Arctic Assault as an escape route if he overextends onto you, not as an opener. Level 3 is your first real window — Q into double-strike Winter's Wrath builds full Frost, and Permafrost stuns him in place; the moment he steps past the minion wave to push you off CS, that combo halves his HP and starts the gank clock. Don't contest his push with your body — contest it with one punishing chain at his overstep, then walk back under tower.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin flip of who steps up first — take W, last-hit, and give him nothing; his Flamespitter is short range but punishing if you stand in it, and Electro Harpoon's slow does nothing while Frost Armor is still up. At level 2 he spikes harder than you: Flamespitter into overheat autos beats your raw auto pattern with no Frost stacks, so use Arctic Assault as an escape route if he overextends onto you, not as an opener. Level 3 is your first real window — Q into double-strike Winter's Wrath builds full Frost, and Permafrost stuns him in place; the moment he steps past the minion wave to push you off CS, that combo halves his HP and starts the gank clock. Don't contest his push with your body — contest it with one punishing chain at his overstep.

edits.before: From level 4 you play the Scrap Shield timer: Rumble's shield and move speed on a 6-second cooldown is what lets him walk away from your engages, so track when he burns it and commit Arctic Assault only when it is down. At level 6, Glacial Prison changes the entire dynamic — throw it when he is positioning for Flamespitter range and it lands before he can react; he has no dash and no real escape, so a clean R into E chain is a guaranteed kill with your jungler. Your lane becomes a gank magnet he can't defuse because he can't safely blow Equalizer under tower pressure without feeding you a free stun window.
edits.after: From level 4 you play two timers. Scrap Shield is a 6-second shield and speed burst that walks him out of your engages, so commit Arctic Assault only just after he spends it — and watch the heat bar, because at full heat Junkyard Titan Overheats him and he cannot cast a single spell until it drains. That lockout is the cleanest engage window this lane offers. At level 6, Glacial Prison changes the dynamic: throw it while he is positioning for Flamespitter range and he has no dash to answer it, so a clean R into Permafrost chain is a kill with your jungler. Your lane becomes a gank magnet he cannot defuse without burning Equalizer under tower.

edits.before: Two items in, your Permafrost uptime and resistances make Flamespitter's sustained DPS irrelevant — he cannot burn through your stacked armor fast enough before you stun and CC chain him. The game is decided by who initiates: throw Glacial Prison before he casts Equalizer and the teamfight is yours; walk into an already-placed Equalizer and even a tank struggles. In side lanes you win the 1v1 cleanly, but stay out of brushes where he can drop the ult zone on your path and fight you through the slow. Group for objectives, find the initiation angle, and let your R plus Permafrost chain turn every Baron and dragon fight into a lock-down massacre.
edits.after: Two items in, your Permafrost uptime and Fury of the North's Frost Armor make Flamespitter's sustained DPS irrelevant — he cannot burn through stacked armour and magic resist fast enough before you stun and chain him. The game is decided by who initiates: throw Glacial Prison before he casts Equalizer and the teamfight is yours; walk into an already-placed Equalizer and even a tank struggles. In side lanes you win the 1v1 cleanly, but stay out of brushes where he can drop the ult zone on your path and fight you through the slow. Group for objectives, find the initiation angle, and let your R plus Permafrost chain turn every Baron and dragon fight into a lock-down massacre.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your Q dash has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Rumble Scrap Shield: 6s — shield and speed on demand, so trade just after he burns it. - The real window is Overheat: at full heat he cannot cast at all. - Equalizer: 130s at rank 1, and it decides who starts the fight.

notes: Slot labels were wrong: the page called Flamespitter (W) and Scrap Shield (E). Flamespitter is Q, Scrap Shield is W, Electro Harpoon is E — and Electro Harpoon appeared nowhere on the page despite being his only ranged tool, with two charges, a slow and magic-resist shred. Two decisive mechanics added: Junkyard Titan's Overheat locks him out of casting entirely at full heat, and Fury of the North's Frost Armor grants slow immunity, so Electro Harpoon's pin does nothing until a hit breaks the armour (the same fact the already-written mirror audits/top/rumble__sejuani.json states from his side). Side values cannot be edited within the +/-10% length band, so this is flagged rather than patched.
